name: Cambodia
system_note: In practice a one-party state run by the Hun family.
snapshot: A cold peace followed the deadly 2025 border war with Thailand, while Cambodia's scam compounds, which hold trafficked workers, drew global crackdowns.
culture: Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world, appears on the flag and anchors Khmer identity. Apsara dance, nearly wiped out under the Khmer Rouge, was rebuilt by surviving dancers. Water festivals and Pchum Ben, when families honour ancestors at pagodas, are central to the year. Cambodian rock of the 1960s is rediscovered by new generations.
society: The Khmer Rouge killed about a quarter of the population between 1975 and 1979, and its legacy still shapes society. Garment exports, tourism and Chinese investment drive growth. Online scam compounds, many tied to Chinese crime groups and holding trafficked workers, became a major industry and a diplomatic liability. The opposition has been dissolved and critics jailed.
situation: The border between Cambodia and Thailand was drawn by French colonial surveyors in 1904-07, and the two countries have fought over the line, and the ancient Khmer temples along it, ever since. In 2025 the dispute exploded into the worst fighting in decades: clashes in July and again in December killed dozens and displaced more than a million people on both sides, and Thai jets bombed casinos and scam compounds inside Cambodia (The Vibes/AFP). Trump brokered a peace accord, which he still cites as one of his successes.

In 2026 the peace is cold. In February Prime Minister Hun Manet, a West Point graduate who inherited the job from his father Hun Sen in 2023, gave his first interview to international media and said Thai forces were occupying Cambodian land "further beyond even Thailand's own unilateral claim," urging Bangkok to let a joint boundary commission resume work (Reuters via NST). In Thailand, Anutin Charnvirakul rode nationalist anger over the war to a landslide in February. Cambodia's other problem is the one Thailand used to justify its strikes: industrial-scale cyber scam compounds, where trafficked workers are forced to defraud people worldwide. Parliament passed a law against the scam rings, and Hun Manet admitted of one accused tycoon, "We did not know that he was the kingpin." Critics note that many compounds are linked to well-connected businessmen. Meanwhile Hun Sen, as Senate president, remains the power behind his son; analysts noted he, not Hun Manet, ran the 2025 war from his "war room."
power: A constitutional monarchy under King Norodom Sihamoni, in practice a one-party state. The Cambodian People's Party holds almost every seat after the main opposition was dissolved in 2017. The Hun family dominates government, the military and business.
holders: Prime Minister Hun Manet, since 2023; Senate President Hun Sen.
